I am 63 years old. I have farmed these 12 mu in Quzhou for 45 years. My mother taught me everything. I never went to school. I cannot read the words on the bags, but I know the pictures and I know my land. My old man and I are two people. We have a well. Last year my wheat made about 1100 jin per mu and my maize made about 1200 jin per mu. I do not change what works. I watch my neighbor Old Li. His family always has good fields.

For winter wheat, I sow in October. I use the same white-seed wheat I have bought from the seed shop for ten years. It is the improved kind, not the old traditional kind. Before sowing, I rotary till the field. I put one full bag of compound fertilizer per mu — the dealer tells me it is 50 kilograms. At green-up time in March, when the wheat turns green, I spread half a bag of urea per mu, about 20 kilograms. I water four times: the wintering water in November, the green-up water in March, the booting water in April when the heads are coming out, and one more at grain filling in May if the sky stays dry. I spray herbicide after sowing, and I spray two more times for bugs and rust in spring, so three sprays total. I expect about 1100 jin per mu this year too.

For summer maize, as soon as the wheat is cut in early June, I plant. There is no time to plough. I plant right into the stubble, no-tillage. I use hybrid corn seed, the red-cob kind Old Li uses, about 4 jin per mu. At sowing, I put 40 jin of compound fertilizer per mu in the furrow. When the plants are knee-high and the ear is forming — what they call the big trumpet stage — I spread 20 jin of urea per mu. I water three times in summer. July is hot and dry and the well must keep up. I spray herbicide at sowing, and I spray for corn borer twice in July and August. I expect about 1200 jin per mu.

Fertilizer is expensive. A big bag of compound is 180 yuan, urea is 110 yuan. I spend about 300 yuan per mu on fertilizer. I would rather spend a little more than risk losing yield. If the harvest fails, I have to borrow money. That is a disaster. Wasting some fertilizer is just a cost. I copy what Old Li does. If he puts more, I put more. I do not trust new ideas unless I see them work on his field first.
